seoTitle: How to Get a Shopify Access Token (Storefront & Admin)
metaDescription: Generate a Shopify Access Token for the Storefront or Admin API by creating a custom app so you can authenticate external integrations.
intro: Custom API integrations and private apps need a Shopify Access Token to authenticate securely with your store. This guide covers how to create a custom app in Shopify, generate an Access Token, and understand the difference between the Storefront and Admin API tokens.

steps.heading: Open your Shopify app settings
steps.body: Go to your Shopify admin's app development section to begin creating a custom app.

steps.heading: Create a custom or private app
steps.body: Set up a new custom app specifically for the integration or script that needs API access.

steps.heading: Configure API scopes
steps.body: Select the specific permissions your app needs, whether for Storefront API or Admin API access.

steps.heading: Generate the Access Token
steps.body: Once configured, Shopify will generate your Access Token, which you'll use to authenticate API requests.

steps.heading: Store the token securely
steps.body: Keep your Access Token private and store it securely, since it grants direct access to your store's data.

faq.question: What's the difference between the Storefront and Admin API tokens?
faq.answer: The Storefront API token is used for public-facing storefront data like products and collections, while the Admin API token grants access to manage store data such as orders and customers.

faq.question: Can I regenerate an Access Token if it's compromised?
faq.answer: Yes, you can revoke and regenerate a new Access Token from your custom app settings if the original one is exposed.

faq.question: Do I need coding knowledge to create a custom app?
faq.answer: Creating the app itself doesn't require coding, but using the Access Token in an integration or script does require development knowledge.

faq.question: Is the Access Token the same as my Shopify password?
faq.answer: No, an Access Token is a separate credential specifically for API authentication and should never be confused with or shared like a login password.
